page.layout: One page of text in a single column of verse, with the page number and running head at the top. A catchword "Hic" stands at the lower right, below the last line.

p.i: Quòd rite veris Numen honoribus, Votisque semper supplicibus colis, Quod inssa[?] feruas, & potenti Te geris vsque Deo minorem.
Quid tuta virtus praesidio Patris Possit supremi, quid queat indoles Addicta Christo, Principisve Quid valeant pia vota iusti
Hostilis ardens agminis impetus Senfit retusus nuper, & aemula Senfere, quae trifti cohortes Cortracia[?] cecidere pugna:
Sensitque Ductor, funera qui tibi Audax parabat dura IOVESIVS: Quum vota rififfet piorum Sollicitasque preces superbus.
Nam vitta spreto Numine brachiis Fidens iuuentus cum Duce corruit: Vicitque cœlestem precatus Miles opem metuendus hosti.
Sic praepotenti Ieffaides prece Pugnauit olim, quum rudis agminum Fudit Philistæas phalanges, Atque trucem feriit Gigantem:
Quem mole vasta corporis ardui Armabat ensis, cuspis & anea Ingentis hastae: cuique pectus Ære ferox solido misabat.

page.notes: The printed word after "inssa" is uncertain (long s and ff forms); "inssa[?]" is a best reading. "Cortracia" may be a misprint for "Contracia"; kept as printed with [?]. "IOVESIVS" is set in small capitals in the original. The "Hic" at lower right is a catchword, not a note. The initial "A" of "Audax" and "Q" of "Quòd" are decorated letters. No greek or hebrew on the page.
